saints.name: St. Edmund Campion
saints.title: Priest and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: An Oxford scholar who became a Jesuit and returned in secret to Elizabethan England, where he was betrayed, racked, and hanged for the faith…
biography: Edmund Campion was born in London in 1540 and rose as one of the most brilliant scholars of Oxford, so promising that Queen Elizabeth herself took notice of him. Drawn to the Catholic faith, he left England, was reconciled to the Church, and in Rome entered the newly founded Society of Jesus, being ordained a priest at Prague.

In 1580 he returned to England on the perilous Jesuit mission, ministering in secret to persecuted Catholics and circulating his bold written challenge to debate. Betrayed and arrested in 1581, he was imprisoned in the Tower of London, repeatedly racked, condemned on a charge of treason, and hanged, drawn, and quartered at Tyburn on 1 December 1581.
saints.knownFor: The most celebrated of the English Jesuit martyrs under Elizabeth I.

canonization.canonized: 1970 by Pope Paul VI, among the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of the Forty Martyrs of England and Wales (vatican.va)
